title: Flintlock SDK: zero-to-prototype pathways
content:
Purpose and audience:
This is a tactical, bias-free quickstart and small-playbook for engineers who want to go from zero to a working prototype with Redwood SDKs (HTTP + node/python examples) in 30–60 minutes. The focus is practical: minimal friction, repeatable checkpoints, and explicit signals for when to escalate to Solutions/SE. This doc is intentionally compact — copyable into a README or a 1-hour workshop script.

Design goals (what this pathway optimizes for):
- Time-to-prototype: shipping a minimal interactive demo in <= 1 hour.
- Observability baseline: a small, high-signal telemetry surface so teams can catch regressions early.
- Fail-fast safety: clear local fallbacks and cost-control defaults.
- Reusability: steps that map to larger production patterns (auth, prompts, rollout flags).

Quickstart checklist (45-minute happy path)
1) Prep (5–10m)
- Create a Redwood account or use an existing org sandbox. Grab API key scoped to sandbox.
- Clone the flintlock-samples repo: git clone https://github.com/redwood-inference/flintlock-samples && cd flintlock-samples/quickstart
- Ensure local env has Node 18+ or Python 3.10+, and Docker installed if you want hermetic local-mode.

2) Install and configure (5m)
- Node: npm install @redwood/sdk (or pip install redwood-sdk)
- Create .env with REDWOOD_API_KEY and REDWOOD_DEFAULT_MODEL (recommended small model for demo). Example:
  REDWOOD_API_KEY=sk-test-xxxx
  REDWOOD_DEFAULT_MODEL=gpt-small-1
- Run a smoke call to confirm connectivity: one-liner curl or SDK snippet below.

3) Minimal app (20–25m)
Goal: interactive REPL/web page that accepts a short user instruction and renders a generated response.
- Node example (Express + SDK):
  const express = require('express')
  const { Redwood } = require('@redwood/sdk')
  const app = express()
  const client = new Redwood({ apiKey: process.env.REDWOOD_API_KEY })
  app.use(express.json())
  app.post('/ask', async (req,res)=>{
    const r = await client.generate({ model: process.env.REDWOOD_DEFAULT_MODEL, prompt: req.body.prompt, max_tokens: 128 })
    res.json({ text: r.text })
  })
  app.listen(3333)
- Python minimal Flask equivalent included in repo.

4) Prompt & UX tuning (5m)
- Ship with 3 sample prompts covering happy, clarifying, and rejection cases.
- Add a simple instruction template for safety: e.g., "If the user asks for medical/legal advice, reply with a safe referral message."
- Keep token limits low for the prototype (max_tokens 128, temperature 0.2).

5) Telemetry baseline (5m)
- Emit: request_id, route (POST /ask), model, latency_ms, token_count, error_code.
- Simple metrics sink: console + lightweight OpenTelemetry collector in repo. Example metric keys: flintlock.requests, flintlock.latency_ms.p50/p95.
- Add one README step: how to turn on DEBUG logging (REDWOOD_DEBUG=true).

6) Local failure modes and safety (continuous)
- Add a local fallback that returns canned help text when API errors or rate limits occur.
- Enforce cost guardrails: reject requests > 256 user tokens; cap concurrent outbound requests to 4 by default.

Staged checkpoints (when to stop and ship vs iterate)
- Checkpoint A (30m): app accepts input, returns plausible model outputs, telemetry streams to console. Demo: show 3 prompts.
- Checkpoint B (60m): add prompt template, a simple client UX (web form), and one telemetry dashboard tab with latency histogram.
- Stop and share: create a short Loom and a PR to sample-apps with instructions for the next owner.

Prompt examples (copy-paste)
- Happy path: "Summarize the following note in 2–3 bullet points:
{user_text}"
- Clarify: "Ask one clarifying question about the user request if it is ambiguous. If it is clear, provide the steps."
- Rejection template (safety): "I’m not able to provide direct legal/medical advice. Here are safe next steps the user can take: ..."

Minimal telemetry spec (1 paragraph)
Every request should produce a compact JSON event (one line) with: timestamp, team (owner), path, model, duration_ms, tokens_in, tokens_out, error (nullable), sample_rate (default 1). Put events on stdout for prototype stage. This yields immediate p50/p95 and a simple regression signal for prompt changes.

SDK test plan (smoke & sentinel tests)
- Local smoke: run quickstart/test/smoke.sh which calls POST /ask and asserts HTTP 200 and presence of text.
- Sentinel prompt test: deterministic prompt that checks for a baseline phrase (used to detect quality/regressions). Keep this in CI with rate limits and allow-list model tags.
- Latency guard: fail CI if p95 > 1200ms in staging for the default model.

Rollout notes (small teams)
- Start internal with feature-flagged route for 10% of users. Keep logs and clipping telemetry at 100 requests/day to lower cost during experiment.
- If quality is stable, increase 10% each day with automated checks on sentinel prompts and error rate.

Common failure patterns and quick remedies
- Empty API key errors: verify .env + correct org permissions. Quick fix: regenerate key and restrict to sandbox.
- High token cost: lower max_tokens and temperature; use condensed prompts or embeddings + retrieval for long contexts.
- Rate-limiting: implement exponential backoff with jitter and a visible client messaging layer.
- Prompt regression after model upgrade: pin model version; run sentinel tests after every model change.

Developer handoff checklist (what to include in a PR)
- README with exactly three run commands (dev, test, build) and a screenshot or short GIF.
- .env.example with minimal keys.
- Smoke and sentinel tests (one-liners).
- Telemetry quickstart: where to toggle DEBUG and where events appear.
- Cost-control knobs documented and enabled by default.

Next steps and follow-ups for Solutions/SE
- If customer intent is production, schedule a 60-minute session: review desired SLOs, expected QPS, dataset size for retrieval, and compliance requirements. Bring: sentinel prompts, sample traffic distribution, and a short Loom of the prototype.

Appendix: quick commands
- Clone & run dev (node): git clone .../flintlock-samples && cd quickstart && npm install && cp .env.example .env && npm run dev
- Smoke test: curl -X POST http://localhost:3333/ask -d '{"prompt":"Summarize the following: ..."}' -H 'Content-Type: application/json'

Notes for maintainers (meta)
- This doc is intentionally portable: it should live as README.md in the flintlock-samples repo and as a short Drive doc for internal run workshops.
- Feedback loop: add comments in this Drive doc and tag eng-developer-experience for prioritization.

Open questions (to resolve before v1)
- Which certified model tag should we recommend as default for PLG demos (cost vs fidelity)?
- Do we want sandbox org keys to auto-expire? (security vs convenience tradeoff)
- Should flintlock quickstarts include a retrieval example by default, or keep retrieval in a second-level lab?

End of doc.
